config.title: useRef Typing

intro.title: useRef Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that uses a button to focus on a text input field. You will learn how to use the useRef hook in TypeScript to create a mutable reference to a DOM element. The core concept is typing useRef to ensure it correctly references an HTML input element, which provides type safety and prevents runtime errors. You will work with React, TypeScript, and TSX files to implement this, focusing on proper type annotations for the ref. This will help you understand how to manage DOM references in a type-safe way within functional components.
intro.usecase: In real-world React applications, properly typed useRef hooks are essential for managing form inputs, interactive dashboards, and complex UI controls. For example, when building a data visualization dashboard, developers use typed refs to directly manipulate chart canvases or control video playback elements without triggering re-renders. In form-heavy applications like admin panels or settings pages, typed refs provide type-safe access to input elements for validation, auto-focus, or measurement tasks. This pattern ensures your component interactions are both performant and type-safe, preventing runtime errors when accessing DOM properties.

objectives: Initialize a typed useRef hook to store a DOM element reference.
Apply TypeScript generics to define the specific type of a mutable ref object.
Bind a typed ref to a JSX element using the ref attribute.
Manipulate DOM properties safely by accessing the current property of a typed ref.
Configure a ref to persist mutable values across renders without causing re-renders.
Integrate typed refs with event handlers to control user interactions.
Construct a component that uses both mutable value refs and DOM node refs with proper typing.

steps.title: Import React and useRef
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules from the React library.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added to the top of the file, enabling the use of React and the useRef hook.
successCriteria: React and useRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React and useRef from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a JSX element.
steps.hint: Define a component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns something valid like a div or fragment.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useRef } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns JSX.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'App' and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check the name and that it returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize a typed ref for DOM element
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a ref using useRef that will hold a reference to an HTMLInputElement. Initialize it with null and provide the proper TypeScript type.
steps.hint: Remember that useRef returns a mutable ref object. For DOM elements, you need to specify the element type (like HTMLInputElement) and initialize with null.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a typed ref for a div element
const divRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a ref variable declared with the correct TypeScript type for an HTMLInputElement, initialized to null.
successCriteria: A ref variable is declared using useRef with type HTMLInputElement and initialized with null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've specified the correct type (HTMLInputElement) and initialized the ref with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ref declaration is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use useRef with the HTMLInputElement type and initialize it with null.

steps.title: Initialize a typed ref for mutable value
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a second useRef hook to store a number value, initialized to 0, with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.hint: Use the same useRef hook but with a number type parameter and initial value of 0.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed ref for a number
const countRef = useRef<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a second ref variable with proper TypeScript typing for storing a number value.
successCriteria: A useRef hook with number type parameter is declared and initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useRef with a number type parameter and initializing it to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Create a useRef hook with number type and initial value 0.

steps.title: Define handler to focus input
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleFocus that calls the focus() method on your DOM element ref's current property.
steps.hint: Create a regular function that accesses ref.current and calls .focus() on it. Remember to check if ref.current exists before calling methods on it.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handler function that can programmatically focus an input element using the typed ref.
successCriteria: A function named handleFocus is defined that calls .focus() on the DOM element ref's current property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named handleFocus and calls .focus() on the DOM element ref's current property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function is not defined correctly. Create a function named handleFocus that calls .focus() on the DOM element ref's current property.

steps.title: Define handler to increment value
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named 'incrementValue' that increments the current value of the mutable number ref by 1.
steps.hint: The function should access the ref's current property and modify it using the increment operator (++).
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'incrementValue' is defined that increments the mutable number ref's current value.
successCriteria: The 'incrementValue' function is defined and modifies the mutable number ref's current property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named 'incrementValue' and increments the mutable number ref's current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment handler isn't defined correctly. Define a function named 'incrementValue' that increments the mutable number ref's current value.

steps.title: Add input element with ref attribute
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an input element with the ref attribute set to the DOM ref you created earlier.
steps.hint: Use JSX syntax: <input ref={yourDOMRef} />. Make sure to use the correct ref variable name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: connecting a ref to an input element
<input ref={inputRef} />
steps.expectedOutcome: An input element will be added to the component's JSX with the ref attribute properly connected to the DOM ref.
successCriteria: ref attribute is set to the DOM ref variable
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the input element has a ref attribute pointing to your DOM ref variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or the ref attribute isn't properly connected to your DOM ref.

steps.title: Add button to focus input and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the div that calls the focus handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on a button element to call your focus handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button that triggers a function
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element appears in the UI that will focus the input when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element is added with onClick attribute wired to the focus handler function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the onClick attribute wired to your focus handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or not properly wired to the focus handler.

steps.title: Add button to increment value and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a second button element after the focus button that displays 'Increment Value' and has its onClick attribute wired to the increment handler function.
steps.hint: Place the new button after the existing focus button, using the same onClick syntax but pointing to your increment handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with a click handler
<button onClick={handleIncrement}>Increment Value</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A second button labeled 'Increment Value' appears next to the focus button, and clicking it will trigger the increment handler.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Increment Value' is added, and its onClick attribute is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check that it has the correct label 'Increment Value' and the onClick is set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment button is missing or not properly wired. Make sure to add a button element with onClick={handleIncrement} and the text 'Increment Value'.

steps.title: Display the current ref value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element that displays the current value of the countRef ref in the UI.
steps.hint: Use JSX to render a paragraph element that shows the value stored in countRef.current.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a ref value in JSX

Current value: {someRef.current}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current numeric value of countRef inside a paragraph element.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that displays the current value of countRef.current.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but it might not be showing the countRef.current value correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or not displaying the countRef.current value.
